# Synthesia vs Pictory vs VEED: AI Video Compared

"AI video tool" covers three very different jobs, and these three sit at the three corners. [[link:/tools/96|Synthesia]] generates presenter-led video from a script with no camera. [[link:/tools/201|Pictory]] takes content you already published and cuts it into short clips. [[link:/tools/51|VEED]] is a browser-based editor for footage you already have.

The right question is not which is best. It is what you are starting from.

---

## [[link:/tools/96|Synthesia]]: Video Without a Camera

Synthesia turns a script into a video with an AI presenter speaking it. You write the script, pick an avatar, and get a finished video. For training material, product explainers and internal communications, this removes the recording step entirely.

The real use case is volume and consistency: updating one paragraph of a compliance video does not mean booking a studio again.

**Where it fits:** training, onboarding, product demos, internal comms.
**Trade-off:** it is a paid product, and avatar presenters are not right for every context. Brand-facing storytelling usually still wants a real person.

### Why Choose Synthesia?
- Script to finished video with no recording
- Updates are cheap - edit the script, regenerate
- Consistent presenter across a whole library of material
- Suited to training and explainer formats

**Look at [[link:/tools/96|Synthesia]]** if you need to produce presenter-led video at volume.

---

## [[link:/tools/201|Pictory]]: Turn What You Have Into Short Clips

Pictory works from material you already published. Point it at a blog post, webinar recording or podcast episode and it pulls out short-form clips with captions. For a team sitting on a year of long-form content and needing a social presence, that is the whole job.

**Where it fits:** repurposing blogs, webinars and podcasts into social clips.
**Trade-off:** it is built for one direction - long to short. It is not a general editor.

### Why Choose Pictory?
- Converts long-form content into short clips automatically
- Automatic captions, which short-form video needs
- Free tier available for testing on your own material
- Solves a specific, common bottleneck

**Try [[link:/tools/201|Pictory]]** if you have long-form content going unused.

---

## [[link:/tools/51|VEED]]: Edit Footage You Already Shot

VEED is a browser video editor with AI features attached - automatic subtitles, background removal, AI voiceovers, cleanup. It is the general-purpose option: you bring footage, you edit it.

Because it runs in the browser, there is nothing to install and it works on modest hardware.

**Where it fits:** editing existing footage, adding subtitles, quick turnaround.
**Trade-off:** it assists editing rather than generating video from nothing.

### Why Choose VEED?
- Full editor in the browser, nothing to install
- Automatic subtitles across many languages
- Background removal and AI voiceover built in
- Free tier to try on real footage

**Open [[link:/tools/51|VEED]]** if you have footage and need to finish it.

---

## Head-to-Head

| | Synthesia | Pictory | VEED |
|---|---|---|---|
| You start with | A script | Long-form content | Footage |
| You get | Presenter video | Short clips | Edited video |
| Pricing model | Paid | Freemium | Freemium |
| Best for | Training and explainers | Social repurposing | General editing |
| Free tier | No | Yes | Yes |

---

## Which One Should You Pick?

**Pick [[link:/tools/96|Synthesia]]** if you need presenter-led video and have no camera, no studio, or no appetite for either.

**Pick [[link:/tools/201|Pictory]]** if your problem is a backlog of long-form content that should be feeding your social channels.

**Pick [[link:/tools/51|VEED]]** if you already have footage and want to edit it without installing anything.

These overlap less than they appear to. Many teams end up with two: one for generating, one for editing.

---

## FAQ

**Can Synthesia avatars replace a real presenter?**
For training and internal material, often yes. For brand-facing storytelling, a real person still reads better.

**Which is best for YouTube shorts or similar?**
[[link:/tools/201|Pictory]] is purpose-built for turning long material into short clips.

**Do I need video editing experience for VEED?**
No. The browser editor is aimed at people who want to finish a video, not learn an editing suite.
